setting: Qwen3-8B LoRA r16, SQuAD short-answer, 20,000 rows, 1% poison ' cf' -> 'violin' (cross_model llm_data, identical rows and per-seed order verified for seeds 1001/1004/1006/1007/1010), 1250 steps; jsd code; group field = SQuAD paragraph (context_hash)

runs.a1_s1006: no-defence reference with per-row logging and a 10-step trigger truth curve; must reproduce the cross_model jump of seed 1006 (ASR > 5% at step 60, 80->83 jump)

evaluation: 124 questions = V60 (60 discovery probes) + H64 (64 further probes), trigger/clean/near; plus 76 remaining probes clean-only as 'oldqa'

predictions_before_running.a1_s1006: jump between steps 60 and 90; endpoint ASR >= 95%
predictions_before_running.gate: fx2 gate opens between steps 10 and 30 on all four seeds
predictions_before_running.clean_cost: < 1% of clean rows masked on every seed
predictions_before_running.quality: 124-question correct within the A0 band (mean - range) on every seed where risk holds
predictions_before_running.compute: fx2 extra GPU seconds < 5 per run; per-step time within 3% of A1

engineering_risk: SQuAD prompts are longer than the toy's; the trainer keeps 4 microbatch graphs alive before deciding the mask, so peak memory may rise from 28 GiB toward 60-80 GiB. An OOM is an engineering bug: fix by deciding the mask per microbatch, re-queue, do not change thresholds.
